description: Key federal regulations, guidance, and policy frameworks governing AI use in higher education

categories.name: U.S. Department of Education Guidance
categories.description: Official federal guidance on AI use in educational settings

sources.title: Dear Colleague Letter on AI in Education
key_points: Guidance on leveraging federal grant funds to improve education outcomes through AI
AI-based high-quality instructional materials are allowable uses
AI-enhanced high-impact tutoring is an allowable use
AI for college and career pathway exploration, advising, and navigation
Emphasizes importance of engaging affected stakeholders, especially parents
Addresses responsible adoption principles including user privacy

sources.title: Supplemental Priority: Advancing AI in Education
key_points: Integrating AI literacy into teaching practices
Expanding AI and computer science education in K-12 and higher ed
Supporting professional development for educators on AI
Using AI to personalize learning and support differentiated instruction
Enhancing classroom efficiency and reducing administrative burdens

sources.title: Executive Order: Advancing AI Education for American Youth
key_points: Directs agencies to support AI education initiatives
Emphasizes preparing students with AI skills for future workforce
Calls for responsible AI integration in educational settings

categories.name: Student Data Privacy Regulations
categories.description: Federal laws protecting student data in AI applications

sources.title: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)
key_points: Protects privacy of student education records
Applies to all schools receiving federal funds
Parents/guardians have rights to access and review records
Written consent required before disclosing PII
AI tools using education records must comply
Students 18+ must consent to disclosure of education records

sources.title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)
key_points: Protects children under 13 from data collection without parental consent
2025 updates require separate consent for data disclosure to third parties
New data retention and deletion requirements
Enhanced oversight of Safe Harbor programs
Schools may provide consent for educational purposes

categories.name: Civil Rights and Bias Prevention
categories.description: Laws preventing discrimination in AI applications

sources.title: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
key_points: Prohibits discrimination based on race, color, or national origin
Applies to AI systems receiving federal funding
AI tools must not perpetuate bias against protected classes
Institutions must audit AI systems for discriminatory outcomes

sources.title: Title IX of the Education Amendments
key_points: Prohibits sex discrimination in education programs
AI systems must not discriminate based on sex/gender
Applies to admissions, financial aid, and academic AI tools

categories.name: Intellectual Property and AI
categories.description: Copyright and ownership guidance for AI-generated content

sources.title: U.S. Copyright Office AI Guidance
key_points: Human-created works are governed under Title VII
Copyright protects original expression created by human authors
Purely AI-generated material is not protected by copyright
Guidance on AI data-scraping of copyrighted material forthcoming

categories.name: Department of Education AI Use Cases
categories.description: Official inventory of AI implementations within the U.S. Department of Education

sources.title: Aidan Chatbot (Federal Student Aid)
key_points: Virtual assistant using natural language processing
Answers common financial aid questions
Over 2.6 million unique customer interactions
Available on StudentAid.gov

sources.title: CAISY - AI Assessment System
key_points: Enhances decision-making and operational efficiency
Delivers real-time insights and predictive analytics
Skillsoft Percipio Assessment integration

sources.title: AWS Bedrock Integration
key_points: Foundation model integration for text generation
Supports summarization and conversational AI
Personalization and content creation capabilities

governance_framework.title: Key Governance Principles for AI in Higher Education

principles.description: Integrate privacy protections into AI systems from the outset, ensuring FERPA and COPPA compliance
Provide clear disclosure about AI use, data collection, and algorithmic decision-making
Maintain human review for high-stakes decisions affecting student outcomes
Regularly audit AI systems for discriminatory outcomes across protected classes
Collect only necessary data and establish clear retention policies
Involve students, parents, faculty, and staff in AI adoption decisions
